flex.latencyPositioning: Variable latency / non-real-time. Utilizes sheddable compute capacity subject to queuing delays that can extend to several minutes.
flex.reliabilityPositioning: Best-effort availability with lower criticality. Under heavy platform load, requests may be delayed or preempted; no automatic upgrade to standard tier.
flex.serviceTierSemantics: Synchronous inference option specified via service_tier: flex parameter in Interactions API and GenerateContent.
flex.timeoutRecommendation: Official documentation explicitly recommends increasing client timeouts to 10 minutes or more to accommodate potential queuing.
flex.pricingRelationship: Cost-optimized with approximately 50% discount compared to standard rates (e.g., 0.15 USD / 1M input tokens vs 0.30 USD standard; 1.25 USD / 1M output tokens including thinking vs 2.50 USD standard).
flex.availabilityConstraints: Available on Gemini models including gemini-3.5-flash-lite via generativelanguage.googleapis.com; requires explicit service_tier flex declaration.

standard.latencyPositioning: Standard predictable on-demand latency, typically low single-digit seconds (2s - 5s) for flash models under normal conditions.
standard.reliabilityPositioning: Standard production availability SLA without sheddable preemption.
standard.serviceTierSemantics: Default tier when service_tier is omitted or explicitly set to standard.
standard.availabilityConstraints: Universally available across standard Gemini API endpoints.

priority.latencyPositioning: Lowest latency and highest queue priority, minimizing queuing delay during peak platform traffic.
priority.reliabilityPositioning: Highest criticality and uptime assurance; overflow requests automatically spill over to standard tier rather than failing.
priority.serviceTierSemantics: Specified via service_tier: priority in request configuration.
priority.pricingRelationship: Premium pricing tier above standard rates.
priority.availabilityConstraints: Available for enterprise / high-criticality workloads on select endpoints.

deepseek.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash under OFF_PEAK pricing window (14 total attempts across Attempt 2 and Final Re-Canary)
deepseek.percentilesDisclaimer: Descriptive only due to sample size (N=14); no statistical confidence claimed.
deepseek.distributionAssessment: Strictly bounded within interactive SLOs; 100% of invocations completed well under 10 seconds (max 9412 ms).

geminiFlex.description: Gemini-3.5-Flash-Lite with service_tier: flex (11 total attempts across Attempt 2 and Final Re-Canary)
geminiFlex.percentilesDisclaimer: Descriptive only due to sample size (N=11); no statistical confidence claimed.
geminiFlex.distributionAssessment: Bimodal heavy-tailed distribution: normal median ~2.6s, but 18.2% (2/11) exhibited extreme tail latency (14535 ms and 15001 ms) due to sheddable compute queueing. Matches official provider tier behavior.

latencyAnalysis.comparativeFinding: The latency divergence between DeepSeek OFF_PEAK (max 9.4s) and Gemini Flex (2 calls >14.5s, 1 timeout) is not an implementation bug or random network glitch. It directly reflects Google official Flex tier architecture: sheddable queueing capacity with potential multi-minute wait times, fundamentally incompatible with a 15-second synchronous interactive failover ceiling.

optionA.name: Keep Gemini Flex as interactive fallback and raise global timeout
optionA.uxImpact: Severely degraded. Interactive users waiting for primary DeepSeek (up to 15s) followed by a lengthened Flex fallback (e.g. 60s-600s) would experience unacceptable 1-10 minute freezes on synchronous UI actions.
optionA.providerTierCompatibility: Incompatible. Violates Google official guidance that Flex is intended for latency-tolerant, non-real-time workloads.
optionA.tailRisk: Extreme. Exposes end users directly to unconstrained queueing spikes and preemption.
optionA.worstCaseDuration: At 120s timeout, 14-invocation canary worst-case runtime reaches 28 minutes; at 600s, up to 140 minutes.
optionA.impactOnPrimarySlo: Unnecessarily weakens DeepSeek interactive SLO by diluting the fail-closed protection.

optionB.name: Keep 15s interactive timeout and replace Gemini Flex with Gemini Standard or Priority
optionB.uxImpact: High. Gemini Standard provides predictable 2-5s response times without sheddable queuing.
optionB.providerTierCompatibility: Fully compatible with Google service-tier definitions for interactive applications.
optionB.costImpact: Standard tier costs ~2x Flex ($0.30/1M vs $0.15/1M input). However, because fallback traffic represents <1% of volume, overall portfolio cost increases by <0.5%.
optionB.downside: Completely abandons the strategic 50% cost savings of Gemini Flex for all workloads, including asynchronous/background jobs.

optionC.name: Split execution into Interactive and Background/Economy lanes
optionC.uxImpact: Optimal. Interactive user requests never encounter sheddable queuing; background jobs benefit from 50% discount.
optionC.architectureSummary: Dual-lane architecture separating strict low-latency interactive routing from asynchronous economy batch routing.

interactiveLane.fallbackCandidate: Separately benchmarked low-latency candidate (e.g., Gemini Standard / Priority)

backgroundEconomyLane.executionModel: Asynchronous queue / background worker, preventing edge HTTP connection timeouts

optionC.complexityAndObservability: Requires explicit routing classification and independent canary matrices, but provides crystal-clear SLO boundaries and operational resilience.

recommendedArchitecture: Dual-Lane AI Routing Architecture: (1) Interactive Lane retaining 15,000ms hard ceiling with DeepSeek OFF_PEAK primary and separately certified low-latency fallback (e.g. Gemini Standard); (2) Background/Economy Lane for latency-tolerant workloads utilizing Gemini-3.5-Flash-Lite Flex with extended timeout (e.g. 300-600s) operating asynchronously.
